editorial:
The Black Sleep is a black-and-white 1956 horror film of about 82 minutes, directed by Reginald LeBorg. It has Basil Rathbone, Akim Tamiroff, Lon Chaney Jr., John Carradine and Bela Lugosi in the cast. A creator would want it for the cast alone, since several well-known horror actors appear together. A copy is listed on the Internet Archive.

The rights trap is that the print's status is not settled. A 1956 film is free only if its notice was missing or its 28th-year renewal was never filed. Here that renewal window was 1983-1984. I did not confirm either point. Until someone searches the Copyright Office records for a renewal, treat the film as possibly still protected. Do not assume a free copy online is cleared. The score and the underlying story are also unchecked.
faq: Is The Black Sleep (1956) safe to reuse in my video?

Not yet. The print's renewal status is unconfirmed, because the Copyright Office renewal search for 1983-1984 has not been run. Search publicrecords.copyright.gov for the title before you use it. If a renewal turns up, the film is still under copyright.
Does an Internet Archive copy mean the film is free to use?
No. Hosting a film on the Internet Archive does not clear its rights. Clear the print's renewal status, the score and the story separately.
